subject: Re: Moving legacy monthly to annual - buy-up options and SLA tradeoffs
messages:
From: Cara Lin <cara@nova-finance.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@nova-finance.com
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Moving our legacy monthly plan to an annual commitment - options

Jonas,

Thanks for taking this. We're exploring a move off our month-to-month plan into an annual prepay to reduce per-unit cost and simplify billing. A few constraints from our side:
- We have three product teams with variable usage; early ramp (months 1-4) will be light.
- Procurement needs predictable GAAP treatment and prefers a multi-year arrangement with step-up discounts.
- We need some breathing room for overages in Q1 while teams ramp.

Could Redwood propose a structure that:
1) Lands us on an annual prepay for year 1 with an option to extend to 3 years for better pricing;
2) Offers a staged ramp (e.g., commit vs expected usage months) and a true-up window;
3) Lists any one-time credits or onboarding concessions for migrating from monthly billing (we already have invoices going back 14 months).

Also need clarity on SLA tradeoffs if we move to a discounted reserved tier.

Appreciate a concrete term sheet and a short timeline for procurement review.

Best,
Cara
Cara Lin
Head of Procurement
Nova Finance

[Attachment: nova_usage_snapshot_q3.csv (text/csv)]

From: jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Cara Lin <cara@nova-finance.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 08:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Moving our legacy monthly plan to an annual commitment - options

Cara — thanks for the clear ask and for sharing the usage snapshot. We can definitely put together a structured offer that balances cost savings with ramp protections and a clean procurement process. High level:

- Short answer: Yes — we can do a 1yr annual prepay with an option to convert to a 3yr committed term at an improved rate.
- Tradeoffs: deeper discounts require more committed dollars; we can surface an intermediate ‘buy-up’ tier that preserves SLA and burst capacity.

I want to align internally on two specifics before a formal term sheet:
1) Your preferred accounting treatment (capex vs opex) — that will influence whether a deferred credit or one-time onboarding credit is preferable.
2) True-up cadence — do you want quarterly true-ups with a 30-day cure, or a single annual true-up?

Laura and Rishi — looping you in to propose numbers and operational guardrails. I pulled the usage file into the deal record.

Next step: Rishi — can you draft two options (Option A: 1yr prepay + renew option; Option B: 3yr committed with step-up discounts and a 60-day annual true-up) and include a recommended onboarding credit? Laura — finance guidance on acceptable concession language please.

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Sales Director, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

[Internal note: deal needs to be packaged so procurement can close quickly — prefer an easily signable term sheet + DocuSign link]

From: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com, rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Moving our legacy monthly plan to an annual commitment - options

Team — quick guidance from finance and pricing:

Constraints from revenue recognition and the comp plan mean we should prefer a structure with:
- Defined committed annual spend (so we can recognize revenue against the prepay),
- A single annual true-up (simpler for Nova's procurement) but allow a short quarterly operational check-in.

Proposed pricing sketches (to put into Rishi's draft):
Option A — 1yr Prepay + 12mo renewal (preferred for Nova's flexibility)
- Commit: $450k prepay for 12 months (based on their 12mo forecast, with 20% headroom).
- Discount: 18% off list for token generation/embedding units.
- Ramp protection: 3-month grace period on volume enforcement; overages billed at 70% of list within grace, then standard overage thereafter.
- Onboarding concession: one-time $25k credit applied to invoice month 1 for billing migration and data export.
- SLA: Standard enterprise SLA retained; burst capacity guaranteed within their committed region — no SLA downgrade.

Option B — 3yr Committed (more aggressive savings, trade-offs on flexibility)
- Commit: $1.2M total committed (billed annually upfront),
- Discounts: Year1 22% off list, Year2 25%, Year3 28% (step-up tied to renewal),
- Ramp protection: 4-month ramp before enforcement; annual true-up with 60-day cure window,
- Onboarding concession: $40k one-time credit + optional invoice deferral for GAAP alignment (finance can provide letter),
- SLA: For larger reserved pools we ask for a slightly longer remediation window (SLA credits increased but response timelines may extend by 2 hours for highest-severity incidents) — call this an operational trade-off that Nova should approve.

Also recommend: add a single ‘bridge credit’ if they convert within 60 days — this addresses perceived risk from moving off monthly. Finance can sign off on up to $40k total concessions if there is a solid 3yr commit.

Rishi — please fold these numbers into a clear term sheet with bullets, points of contact for legal and procurement, and attach two versions of the term sheet (1yr/3yr). I'll greenlight the concessions once the term sheet shows the cash flow schedule.

Thanks,
Laura
Laura Bennett
VP, Strategic Accounts & Pricing
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: redwood_prepay_term_sheet_v3.pdf (application/pdf) — draft placeholders for both options]

From: jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Cara Lin <cara@nova-finance.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com, procurement@nova-finance.com
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 16:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Moving our legacy monthly plan to an annual commitment - options

Cara — thanks again for the speedy turnaround. Attached is a clean term sheet with two distinct paths (1yr prepay with renewal option; 3yr committed). Summary of our recommended path (Option A — recommended for lower operational risk):

- First year commitment: $450,000 prepay (annual invoice)
- Effective discount: 18% off list for generation and embedding units
- Ramp protection: 3-month grace period, overages billed at 70% list during grace
- Onboarding concession: $25,000 one-time credit applied to first invoice for billing migration and export support
- True-up: Annual true-up with 30-day cure (we will provide quarterly operational reports)
- SLA: No downgrade of enterprise SLA; we preserve burst capacity within committed region

If you prefer a deeper discount and are willing to lock a 3yr commit we can move to Option B (see attached) which increases discounts and adds a $40k onboarding credit plus flexibility on invoice timing. Option B does include a modest SLA remediation-time tradeoff (two-hour extension on highest-severity response window) which we call out explicitly in the term sheet.

Next steps:
- I attached the term sheet and a redlined DocuSign link: please review with procurement and circle back with preferred option and any redlines by Dec 8.
- If helpful, we can schedule a 30-minute procurement + finance call early next week to walk through the GAAP/accounting treatment for the onboarding credit.

Thanks — happy to jump on a call.

Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Sales Director, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: redwood_prepay_term_sheet_v3.pdf (application/pdf)]
